- `code/results/` result files (the section "Result files delivered so far" below says, per file, what it was computed on and which interval is which).

## Data and model (pinned)
- Benchmark: MMLU-Pro (`TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro`, revision `b189ec765aa7ed75c8acfea42df31fdae71f97be`, `test` split, 12,032 items).
- Pool: 1,500 evaluation items drawn uniformly at random without replacement from the test split (seed 0, no length cap, all 14 subjects), plus 12 short demonstration items from 12 different subjects that are not in the evaluation pool (`src/make_pool.py`). The population every real-data number refers to is this pool as an iid sample of MMLU-Pro, for this model and this configuration space; not MMLU-Pro at large and not other models.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`, revision `989aa7980e4cf806f80c7fef2b1adb7bc71aa306`, float32, CPU. Scoring is direct answer: the log-probability of each option letter after the answer cue (no sampling, no chain of thought); a cell is correct if the highest-scoring valid letter is the key.
- Configuration space (K = 128 = 4 x 2 x 8 x 2): demonstration set (none, A, B, C; 3 items each) x option labelling (`A.` or `(A)`) x instruction wording (8) x answer cue (2). Wordings and cues are listed in `code/src/harness.py`. Configuration id c = g*16 + m with g = 2*set + label, m = 2*instruction + cue. The pre-specified default (untuned) configuration is c = 0 (no demonstrations, `A.` labels, wording 0, cue 0).
- The cached prefix/item/suffix computation reproduces an uncached forward pass to 6e-5 in log-probability (`code/src/check_harness.py`).

## Truth, uncertainty, seeds
- Truth for the configuration selected on a search set S is its accuracy on the pool items outside S (N - n items, SE about 0.013). S is a uniform random subset of an iid pool, so pool minus S is a fresh iid sample given S. In synthetic and semi-synthetic worlds the exact accuracy is used.
- Uncertainty on real data: between-pool item bootstrap (200 replicates, items resampled with multiplicities; truth excludes every copy of a search item). Intervals labelled `pool-bootstrap` use the replicate-level estimates with the Monte-Carlo variance of the S draws removed (`code/analysis/intervals.py`); spread over S draws is labelled `S-draw-spread`.
- Seeds: every script derives its generators from fixed integer lists (see `np.random.default_rng([...])` calls); the pool uses seed 0.

cd /hutian/repo/paper; cat > sections/discussion.tex <<'EOF'
\section{Discussion and limitations}
\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{What to log and report.}
Log the item-level correctness of every configuration evaluated, declare the candidate space before the search, and report the max-t lower bound over the declared space together with $n$, $B$ and $\Keff$.
In our measurements this bound is valid under random search, hill climbing and successive halving, is narrower than the held-out and Bonferroni bounds, and costs no items; reported scores, by contrast, overstated the gain from tuning several-fold at $n\le100$ and ranked a larger search above a smaller one in more than half of the comparisons that had no true difference.
When items are cheap, a held-out split is also reliable here: it cost at most $0.0025$ in deployed accuracy.

\paragraph{Scope.}
The numbers describe one model of 1.5B parameters, one benchmark, and one configuration space of $128$ choices of demonstrations, format, wording and cue, scored by the log-probability of an answer letter.
The space has no generated or chain-of-thought outputs and no programs of several model calls, so how the gap behaves for such pipelines is not measured.
The pool has $1500$ items, which sets the floor on the fresh-item noise ($0.012$--$0.014$) and makes the largest search size ($n=400$) a large share of it.
The model is weak on this benchmark (mean accuracy $0.27$) and the true spread of configuration accuracies is small ($0.014$), so a tuned configuration gains at most $0.025$ over the default; the gap is therefore close to the pure-noise optimism, and a space with larger true differences would shrink it relative to the prediction, as in the synthetic arm.
All search procedures are replayed on a cached matrix, not run with a real search tool, and the search-log predictor and the bounds are validated for the searchers we replayed.
The generative model extends the measurements beyond $n\le200$ and $K\le128$ only to the extent of its validation checks, which have wide intervals and do not discriminate between the models of dependence.
EOF

  - At n ≤ 100 the reported improvement over the default is at least four times the real one.

- **Waiting on `figtab-repo` (#3):** Fig 4, Fig 5 and Tab 2 on the real arm. Their current versions show only the synthetic arm, from before `protocols_real` landed. Their README says these are not drawn yet.
